newsitem.title: TURKEY: Mitsubishi unit in $1.5 bid for Turkey plant.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi unit in $1.5 bid for Turkey plant.

text.p: A consortium led by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd presented the lowest bid in Turkey's 1,400 MegaWatt coal-fired power plant tender, with a $1.51 billion offer, Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan said on Wednesday.
"The consortium led by Mitsubishi Heavy Industry gave the lowest bid for the Afsin-Elbistan B thermal power plant," Kutan told a news conference.
He said the consortium included U.S. Babcock Lentjes, Mitsubishi Corp, Turkey's Gama, Tekfen, Tokar and Enka.
The other bidders and their price offers for the power plant were as follows:
--Austrian Energy and Environment, Siemens, Toshiba, Caillard, Turkey's Nurol, Simko and Yuksel with $1.77 billion.
--ABB, Siemens, GEC, Alsthom , Nissho Iwai, Turkey's Kutlutas, Guris and Dogus with $1.62 billion.
--Stone & Webster, Steinmuller, Philipp Holzmann with $2.53 billion.
"It will take us about five months to assess the bids fully and come up with the result," Kutan said.
He said the lowest bid price alone was not the only criterion during the assessment.
"We will also look at how they will filter the chimneys against sulphur and other waste gases," he said.
According to the tender terms, the winner of the tender should build a gas filter with a 99-percent efficiency and desulphuriser with a 95-percent efficiency.
"Another thing we will look to is the proportion of Turkish companies in the consortia. The Mitsubishi consortium has the highest Turkish company contribution with 27 percent," Kutan said.

The Afsin-Elbistan B power plant, which will have four units each of 350 MW capacity, will exploit lignite coal in the Elbistan area, which has almost half of Turkey's total lignite reserves of 8.2 billion tonnes.

The plant, to be fully financed by the national power producer TEAS, will produce about eight billion kiloWatt-hours (kWh) annually, against a national power shortfall of about 2.5 billion kWh for 1997.
There is another coal-fired power plant at the same site with a capacity of 1,360 MW.
Turkey has been importing electricity from Iran, Georgia and Bulgaria since late 1996.
